verdict.tagline: Atmospheric New York streets hide punishing fights and frustrating launcher requirements.
for_you_if: you love exploring snowy dystopian cityscapes
you enjoy tackling difficult team combat encounters

claims.claim: Reviewers praise the winter New York setting for its atmospheric, abandoned, and detailed visual design.

citations.review_text: Just started it, have absolutely zero background about it, and it feels like something special, i love the environment, the atmosphere, the graphics, the gameplay, all of these so far feel very very polished and I'm actually engaged which is not something i feel as often as i used to.

This game has one of the best “empty city after everything went wrong” atmospheres I’ve ever seen. Snowy New York looks beautiful, cold, abandoned, and kind of depressing in the perfect way. You walk through the streets and it feels like the city is still alive, just very tired and covered in Christmas decorations that missed the apocalypse memo.

I really like the mix of cover shooting, loot, skills, and slow character progression. You clear missions, upgrade your base, improve your gear, and slowly turn your agent from “guy with a jacket and problems” into someone who can actually survive the city for more than five minutes.

Co-op is where it shines the most. Running missions with friends, healing each other, pushing through tough fights, and getting better loot has that classic “one more run” feeling. And then there’s the Dark Zone, which is basically a trust issue simulator with better jackets. You go in for loot, meet other players, and immediately start asking yourself if humanity was a mistake.

It’s stylish, atmospheric, tense, and still one of the coolest looter-shooter settings out there. The winter New York vibe alone makes it worth playing.

old game, played it on uplay and just bought it on steam on sale. 
old game but still looks amazing, optimized, and pretty solid. ran it 4k native, 120, basically almost max minus 1 or 2 thing set to high.

I completed this game in 2020 when Ubisoft gave it away for free. Later, I bought it on Steam as part of a collection during a sale and revisited the game. It’s a third-person shooter focused on combat, cover mechanics, and gear upgrades. Stronger enemies require a tactical approach, and skills are unlocked by improving your base. The game is well optimized and runs stably even on older systems.

The atmosphere is one of its highlights. Snow-covered streets, empty buildings, and small details like footprints make the world feel realistic. Music and sound design add to the immersive setting. Combat is solid, though the story and characters are less memorable. Endgame mostly focuses on collecting better gear, which may feel repetitive for some players.

Overall, it’s a well-made action RPG with strong gameplay, immersive environments, and stable performance.

After this update, the game feels like it's from 2026! The graphics and lighting are incredible, all movement in the game is unbelievably smooth and amazing, gun sounds, reloads, and weapon swapping are perfect, even the pistol comes out of the Hustler and goes back perfectly, the day and night cycles are stunning, the camera and all the details are flawless—can’t believe this game is from 2016! 10/10 without a doubt!

claims.claim: The shooting combat features enemies that function as bullet sponges with large health bars.

citations.review_text: The shooting feels satisfying, and there’s a great feeling of progression as you constantly find better weapons, gear, and upgrades. There’s always something to chase, whether you're improving your character, upgrading your base, or hunting for better loot. The missions can be especially fun with friends. The game isn't perfect, though. Some enemies can feel like bullet sponges, and the grind for better gear can definitely get repetitive. But overall, The Division does a great job combining third-person shooting, RPG progression, exploration, and co-op gameplay.

The only thing that made me keep playing this is the atmosphere and the graphics. Besides that its just another looter shooter and more importantly just another ubislop game. The problem is the enemies and the gameplay. They focused so much on the atmosphere that the game turns into a walking sim. Not to mention the enemies are complete bullet sponges. It gets repetitive very early on. The story is extreme mid and easily forgettable. The DLCs themselves are not all that special too. Get it only if you play co-op and like ubisoft games and it is on sale. SIngleplayer is decent but it is pretty clear that it was made with co-op in mind.

Edit: This game grows on you. The best advice that I can give is you is that do the side content first. In the order: Encounters -> Side Missions -> Upgrade Missions -> Main Missions. You might get tired of doing this, but it just makes the other missions easier and more fun. In short grind before each main mission.

The Division has a lot of good things going for it. The graphics are impressive, the atmosphere is great, and the story has an interesting idea and setting.

However, the gameplay details really hurt the experience. The biggest issue is the RPG-style health bar system: shooting an enemy multiple times just to see a health bar slowly go down until they finally die feels unrealistic and out of place for a game that presents itself as a tactical military shooter.

This kind of mechanic makes the combat feel more like a fantasy game than a realistic war scenario. A game with the Tom Clancy name should focus more on realism, strategy, and immersive combat instead of turning enemies into damage sponges.

A beautiful game with a great concept, but some gameplay choices take away from the realism and immersion.

I'll be honest - the only thing that keeps me hooked on this game is the atmosphere. That snowy, desolate New York City is absolutely breathtaking. The visuals, the sound design, the little stories told through abandoned apartments and scattered notes... it's pure immersion. And the music? Man, that song on the radio, "Gone to Sleep," is absolutely perfect for this world. It's haunting, emotional, and fits the mood of a city falling apart perfectly. That track alone got me every single time it played.

The mission design, though? Classic "go here, grab that, come back" routine. Lazy and repetitive.

But here's what really stings. This game is basically dead now. The online population is tiny, and finding random teammates is next to impossible. I don't have any friends to squad up with, so I went in solo, fully knowing what I was getting into. And let me tell you, it's rough. Enemies are bullet sponges, you get swarmed constantly, and the difficulty is clearly balanced for a full team. Playing alone feels like an uphill battle from start to finish.

And yet, despite all that, I actually love this game. I keep coming back to it. Not for the quests, not for the combat, but for that world and that music. They pull me in every time, no matter how frustrating the rest gets. Yeah, I suffer through it, but somehow I still enjoy the ride.
Fun and enjoyable but the bullet sponge enemies drive me insane

claims.claim: Enemies require shooting multiple magazines to defeat, while the player character feels fragile.

citations.review_text: Eh, good story decent gameplay but I mainly hate how the enemies are damage sponges and you are as brittle as a leaf.

The Division is a good game but its good doesn't outweigh its bad as much as I wish they did.

The game is one hell of a looker. The ground is can be so watery and the snow texture feels so real you can almost feel its touch. How the snow accumulates on your character and how it blows throw the wind, so many physics based interactable objects, surprisingly detailed indoor areas and the most important - CAR DOORS. The doors close as soon as you interact with it and the devs made sure you realize this by opening every fricking car door imaginable.

Each story mission feels unique in its environment. Of course, thats how it should be but the world can look so same-y and side missions are so repetitive that it feels extremely refreshing when you are playing through a story mission.

That's where my pros ends. The traversal in this game is a snoozefest. You have to travel from A to B on foot, always. There are no vehicles, which I understand given the story of the game, but surely they could've added some gear mods or buffs which increased your movement speed by 10-15% after sprinting for 5 seconds? If your game in encouraging fast travel more than normal means of traversal then it has failed in delivering an engaging world and a decent movement system.

And hoolyyy, enemies are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bullet sponges. We played every main mission on Hard and it took almost 2 or sometimes even 3 AR mags to kill an enemy. I get we played on hard, I get this game is RPG first and foremost but what is the AI doing? Enemies keep spamming you when you are behind cover so as soon as you get out to shoot back, you get slapped in the face by bullets and get knocked out. The other enemies keep rushing you on your position and there's nothing you can do except pray to god. How are we supposed to kill 3 enemies rushing at us, point blank, they only need a few bullets to knock us out and require 2-3 mags to go down? Perhaps you are suggesting using a shotgun? How will I deal with enemies wh…

Tom Clancy’s The Division — Back when entering the Dark Zone felt like signing a contract with bad decisions. Snow-covered streets, endless loot, and enemies who somehow survived three magazines to the face. You came for the tactical shooter, stayed for the loot addiction, and left because a rogue agent ruined your day 🎯
Helpful tip: trust your build, not random teammates.
8.5/10 — came for New York, stayed for the grind.

claims.claim: Combat controls feel clunky, with issues regarding entering and exiting cover or accidentally vaulting during fights.

citations.review_text: The division is an initially fun looter-shooter that quickly becomes very dry and monotonous. Side missions are copy paste missions repeatedly used in different areas. Leveling up takes extremely long, requiring you to do these boring side missions to prepare for the main missions. Many of the enemies are extremely tanky and will push you while firing, giving you no chance to fight back. Other enemies will throw grenades forcing you to move positions causing you to get caught in the open and die These enemies wouldn't be as much of an issue if the cover in combat areas was better designed to allow for easy maneuvering. The player movement is also very janky, many times my character would not do what I wanted them to do while trying to change positions and get brutally punished.

The game has a fantastic storyline and great playability as far as interesting missions and concepts. The overall controls SUCK ASS!!!! Once your in cover it doesn't always let you out of cover. it tries to put you in cover when you are trying to jump over a wall. or it won't let you jump because the CTRL function for jumping won't show let you use it. if you're in cover changing grenades make you jump over the cover and into enemy fire. When you are aiming for headshots you don't get headshots, you have to shoot to damage the enemy enough to get a headshot. So most you have to hit at least 3 times first then you can headshot them. Hitting the enemy fuel tanks requires consecutive shots. Hitting the tank, then the enemy and then the tank resets the damage done to the tank requiring two consecutive shots at least and only on the tiny red part on top of the tank in most instances. Eventually you completely quit playing the campaign because the controls are too inconsistent and glitchy.

claims.claim: Side missions and open-world activities are repetitive and consist of copy-and-paste tasks.

citations.review_text:
A fun and decent start to a series, The Division is a mediocre Looter Shooter hindered by Ubisoft's typical gameplay loops and quirks.

Pro:
-Visually this game still holds up well 10 years later
-Gameplay feels tight, engaging and fun
-Story concept is interesting and sets it apart from other apocalyptic stories.
-RPG and Looter Shooer mechanics are fun albeit shallow and surface level.
- Voice Acting of all the characters do a servicible job.
-Collectibles like the Echo logs add a lot to the backstory and characters

Cons:
-DLC is heavily focused on the endgame Dark Zone PvPvE content that I'm not at all into, so I never bothered engaging with it.
-Narrative delivery is paper thin, very little to no cutscenes all context of story elements are mostly delivered via radio communication messages to the player
-Side content is your typical Ubisoft open-world bland and repetitve "kill x, fetch x, Defend x" without any depth or meaning,
-Collectibles are obtained by being in proximity or engaging in in all the side missions and encounters with the help of a base of operations upgrade that reveals them all on the map for each distract
-No diversity in it's main stories mission structure, literally the exact same concept as it's side content which leaves a ton to be desired.

Overall: I enjoyed the gameplay and getting the collectibles that enhances worldbuilding and backstory of characters and events that are prevalent to the central conflict albeit it was time consuming and tedious after a while. The story's concept is interesting but the narratives delivery leaves a lot to be desired. A decent start to a series and a passable looter shooter but nothing I could rave or recommend unless you have nothing else to play or just wanting a mindless game to sink yourself into for a few days. I'm curious to see what changes or improvements are featured in The Division 2 but as of right now with The Division 1, it's an okay game.

From what I've read, the division 1 is harder in this aspect.

What an absolute slog. 40 hours to get through most of the story and side missions and hunt down a bunch of the collectibles. The movement doesn't feel great, and the map is frustratingly closed off. It's also incredibly repetitive, with very little new information or plot development across the story missions, some of which I'd sworn I'd done before because the environment and objectives were so similar.

The store description doesn't do a very good job of explaining what this game actually is. It's an online, multiplayer-only title, where you'll spend most of your time playing alone in your own session. Unless you actively matchmake to play cooperatively with friends or strangers. The only places you will ever see other players are in the "social hubs", like safe houses and PvP-enabled areas. Otherwise, the social aspect of the game is pretty much useless.

As for the gameplay, it's a tactical looter-shooter. You roam a desolated yet beautiful New York City in winter, killing enemies and scavenging for better loot to optimize your loadout for different situations. Up until the post-game (when you finally hit level 30), the game heavily punishes you if you aren't tactical enough or if you are too conservative with your gear. It has a solid foundation, and it becomes much easier and far more fun once you reach the endgame.

Outside of combat, your goal is to rebuild a Base of Operations across three specialized wings. Each upgrade grants a new perk or ability. You'll have to gather resources to fund these upgrades, which are rewarded by completing campaign missions, side missions, and encounters scattered throughout manhattan.

The campaign itself is nothing stellar, it just works. However, the side content is not great at all. It is repetitive, tedious, and barely interesting especially when playing solo. Every single district features the exact same formula: three side missions and five encounters, and they all play out identically. You'll play the same mission several time, but at a different place, and it's not even well made.

The city itself looks fantastic, atmospheric, and nails the winter pandemic-apocalypse vibe. But, it quickly becomes monotonous as you notice how many assets and street layouts are simply copied and pasted. Ultimately, this is not really a great game. It can be fun enough if you don't take it too seriously, or if you have a group of friends…

One of the most atmospheric and addictive looter-shooters ever made!

Even years after its release, Tom Clancy's The Division remains an absolute masterpiece in terms of world-building and atmosphere. The recreation of a winter, post-pandemic Manhattan is breathtaking. Walking through the snow-covered, desolate streets filled with abandoned cars, Christmas decorations, and dense fog creates a hauntingly beautiful and immersive vibe that no other game has managed to duplicate.

The gameplay loop is incredibly addictive. It perfectly blends tight, cover-based third-person shooter mechanics with deep RPG elements. Customizing your agent, unlocking skills by rebuilding the Base of Operations, and constantly hunting for better weapons and gear sets kept me hooked for dozens of hours. The combat is tactical and challenging, making every encounter with enemy factions feel intense.

And then, there is the Dark Zone. It is easily one of the most brilliant and nerve-wracking multiplayer concepts in gaming history. Entering this high-risk area to hunt for the best loot while constantly looking over your shoulder, never knowing if another player is going to help you or betray you at the extraction point, delivers a pure adrenaline rush.

Whether you play it completely solo or team up with friends in co-op, this game is an unforgettable tactical journey. A true gem!

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the survival mode achievement requires completing multiple runs, which can feel repetitive.

citations.review_text:
Tom Clancy’s The Division:

Is still a fun game overall, but the full achievement experience depends a lot on which content you are playing.

The base game is the best part for me. The setting is great, with New York hit by a deadly outbreak and the city falling apart. The snowy streets, abandoned buildings, enemy factions, loot, cover-based shooting, and Dark Zone all give the game a strong atmosphere. The gameplay loop is simple but fun, and the achievements feel natural and easy to get. Most of them come from just playing the game, doing missions, exploring, upgrading your Base of Operations, and working through the content.

The Underground DLC is also fun, but it is more of a grind. Going below New York into tunnels, stations, and enemy hideouts fits the world really well, and it gives you more PvE content to play after the main game. The achievements are not too bad, but you will be repeating Underground runs for progress, so it can start to feel long if you are only there for completion.

Then there is Survival. All I can say is: hell. The idea is actually really cool. You are sick, cold, undergeared, stuck in a snowstorm, and trying to survive long enough to extract. The atmosphere is amazing, but the achievement hunt was painful. Between failed runs, time investment, difficulty, and frustration, Survival was easily the worst part of the 100% for me.

Overall, The Division is still worth playing, especially for looter-shooter fans, co-op players, casual players, and achievement hunters. The base game is an 8/10, Underground is a 6/10, and Survival is a 2/10 for me.

As a full package: fun game, great atmosphere, mostly good achievements, but Survival is pain.

Great game I would recommend! The story missions are fun and the voice acting is much better than I expected it to be. The game is beautiful especially for it age and the post game content is fun and adds a different variety. The underground was interesting and didn't overstay its welcome. The survival mode on the other hand required way to many runs if you want to 100% the game. By the end of your runs you will know the exact route nodes and enemies you will have to path through. Overall the game is one I really enjoyed coming back to after so many years. There are some collectathon aspects but if the side aspects of the game seem fine the main aspects justify the pricetag of the game.

Great game, loads of content, the worldbuilding is better than the second game imo. I just enjoyed playing this the Division 1 more. 
1 persistant annoying thing on PC, the game often forces windowed mode on launch which is kind of annoying, not as bad as Division 2 though, which for me enables HDR every launch, washing out the game.
The hardest achievment "For the Hoarder..." will take minimum 17 successful runs of survival (1 run is usually 30-60 min, depends how good you are.) which is a slog and a half but is still very much doable for a nice 0.1% achievment.
Best of luck Agent.

citations.review_text:
[h1] The Open World Tactical Cover Shooter that No One Asked for, but Everyone Secretly Wanted. [/h1]

The Division is a Third Person Open World Tactical Cover-Based Looter Shooter with RPG elements and an enduring endgame. Celebrating it's 10th anniversary this year, the game still has plenty to offer. Granted it has some stability issues (especially with Dx12), PvP / PvPvE is rife with hackers, and it has a LOT of balancing issues (especially in the higher difficulty endgame). Nonetheless, the game is gorgeous, runs smooth for the most part, and also features some of the most satisfying tactical combat I have ever experienced.

[h2] BEFORE YOU PLAY: [/h2]

-Stability: This game has some very annoying stability issues. Every now and then, my grapics drivers will simply crash, and there is no other way to fix it than to reboot my PC. At first it was sparse enough to not be a problem (it would happen every 3 or 4 days), but it quickly got to the point where it was crashing twice daily, and it very much detracted from the overall experience. This has also been a common problem for years apparently. I have tried multiple proposed solutions: Switching to Dx11, going windowed mode, tuning graphics settings left and right - nothing worked. And no, my GPU is fine. I ran multiple diagnostics on it and all of them came back clean. Temps never even rose above 69 degrees C while gaming. I use an RX 580 by the way.

[h2] Abstract [/h2]

-It feels amazing to shoot stuff!
-RPG elements keep you coming back for more.
-Great weapon customisability.
-Music is very good.
-Open World Manhattan is very cool.
-Cool Spy gadgets and tech.
-Massive build variety to choose from.

-Game is very unbalanced at higher difficulties.
-Movement and aiming have a bit of a learning curve.
-NOT ENOUGH STORAGE!
-Stability issues (see above).
-Too much loot to sift through (99.9% is scrapped).
